items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-01
items.q: I can remember Herman Sherman telling me how to, well, we would get sandwiches

ctx.x: Yeah, they, these groups, the parade tended to stop at, oh, pretty regular intervals. Frequently at a bar or a bar and grocery combination place. Mm-hmm. Sometimes at private homes. Mm-hmm. And basically they would turn in more or less in military fashion, usually in the single file, uh, flanking movement. And the band would circle together on the sidewalk, as a rule, or just out in the street. Mm-hmm. And play while the group went inside. And then the band and the second line would relax outside while the…

I can remember Herman Sherman telling me how to, well, we would get sandwiches that were wrapped up in wax paper, as I remember it. And he'd show me how to slip them down in my umbrella. I'd have this umbrella which was, so you'd have plenty of sandwiches. Well, I mean, umbrellas were very useful things. I never thought of that purpose. No. It's just one of those little things that just came back to it.
Obviously, obviously you can't roll your brawly very tightly if you're carrying sandwiches. No, it was very loose, in fact.
